newsitem.title: CHINA: Price Waterhouse has member firm in Beijing.
newsitem.headline: Price Waterhouse has member firm in Beijing.

text.p: International accountancy firm Price Waterhouse has admitted a Chinese accounting firm in Beijing as a member of its world operations, world chairman Dominic Tarantino said on Friday.
The move is a response to changes in Chinese regulations that encourage international accounting firms to move away from joint ventures, Price Waterhouse officials told reporters.
The Chinese member firm is Zhang Chen Certified Public Accountants, a recently licensed company formed by Chinese nationals associated with Price Waterhouse.
The move makes Price Waterhouse the first of the big six international accounting firms to use this structure in China, Tarantino said.
"It is a very important step towards one of our objectives -- of building a Chinese-led national practice," he told reporters.

Price Waterhouse has had a joint venture in Shanghai since 1992 but China has ordered the disbanding of accounting joint ventures over the next five years in a move aimed partly at making its accounting sector more independent.
In the past, foreign companies have formed joint ventures with state-run companies that often have been too closely linked with local government interests.
Price Waterhouse officials said authorities in Beijing were aware of the need for independent professional accountants and that they wanted such firms to be private.
Price Waterhouse officials said its Shanghai joint venture would have to be reorganised before it could become a member firm
